changes.title: New legitimate interest justifications added throughout data use table
changes.new_excerpt: It is in our and our users' legitimate interests to expand our product features and deliver additional services that enhance platform functionality
changes.explanation: The policy adds multiple new statements explaining the 'legitimate interests' legal basis Anthropic relies on for various data processing purposes, such as expanding features, marketing, investigating misconduct, handling complaints, security, and service reliability. These appear to be added explanatory text rather than changes to what data is collected.
changes.practical_effect: Users gain more detail about why Anthropic believes it is legally permitted to process their data for these purposes, without changes to what data is actually used.

changes.title: New legitimate interest basis for direct marketing
changes.new_excerpt: It is in our legitimate interests to promote our Services that may be of interest to you, including sending direct marketing.
changes.explanation: A new justification is added stating that sending direct marketing to users is based on Anthropic's legitimate interests rather than a different legal basis.
changes.practical_effect: This clarifies the legal basis under which users may receive marketing communications from Anthropic.

changes.title: New legitimate interest basis for addressing illegal activity and cooperating with authorities
changes.new_excerpt: It is in our legitimate interests to protect our business, employees and users from illegal activities, inappropriate behavior or violations of terms that would be…
changes.explanation: A new statement explains that protecting against illegal or inappropriate behavior and cooperating with authorities is justified as a legitimate interest, alongside an added note of a duty to cooperate with authorities.
changes.practical_effect: This provides more explicit disclosure that Anthropic may share information with authorities as part of addressing illegal or inappropriate conduct.

changes.title: New legitimate interest basis for handling complaints
changes.new_excerpt: It is in our legitimate interests to fully understand and make reasonable efforts to resolve customer complaints in order to improve user satisfaction.
changes.explanation: A new explanation clarifies the legal basis for processing data related to customer complaints, also noting a legal obligation may apply in some cases.
changes.practical_effect: Users are given more detail about how and why their complaint-related data may be processed.

changes.title: New legitimate interest basis for security monitoring
changes.new_excerpt: It is in our legitimate interests to protect user data and our systems from intrusion or compromise through monitoring and swift response.
changes.explanation: A new statement adds justification for security-related data processing based on legitimate interests and a legal obligation to maintain adequate safeguards.
changes.practical_effect: This clarifies the basis for security monitoring activities that involve user data but does not indicate a change in the monitoring itself.

changes.title: New legitimate interest basis for service reliability and error correction
changes.new_excerpt: It is in our legitimate interests to maintain continuous functioning of our services and rapid correction of problems to ensure a positive user experience
changes.explanation: A new explanation is added clarifying the legal basis for processing data to maintain service functionality and fix errors.
changes.practical_effect: This adds transparency about why Anthropic processes data for debugging and reliability purposes.

changes.title: Expanded description and apparent separation of model-training research purpose
changes.new_excerpt: Our research also benefits the AI industry and society: it investigates the safety, inner workings, and societal impact of AI models
changes.old_excerpt: To improve the Services and conduct research (including model training). See our Non-User Privacy Policy for more details on the data used to train our…
changes.explanation: The policy restructures and expands the explanation of research purposes, splitting what was previously a single combined purpose (service improvement and research, including model training) into separate entries, one of which explicitly excludes model training and another that explicitly includes it, each with added justifications about benefits to users, the AI industry, and society.
changes.practical_effect: Users can better distinguish between data used for general service/feature improvement versus data used specifically for training AI models, though the overall scope of research-related data use does not appear reduced.

changes.title: New legitimate interest basis for enforcing Terms of Service outside contract performance
changes.new_excerpt: It is in our legitimate interests to enforce the rules and policies governing use of our services, to maintain intended functionality and value for users.
changes.explanation: A new clause explains that outside of contractual performance, Anthropic may rely on legitimate interests to justify processing data for enforcing its Terms of Service and usage policies.
changes.practical_effect: This provides additional legal justification for data processing related to enforcement actions, such as account restrictions or investigations into policy violations.

report.summary: Anthropic's Privacy Policy was updated primarily to add detailed explanations of the 'legitimate interests' legal basis it relies on for various data processing activities, including marketing, security, complaint handling, service reliability, and enforcement of terms. It also restructured and expanded the description of research-related data use, including model training, providing more specificity about the purposes and societal justifications of such research.

changes.title: Cross-service data sharing for personalization
changes.new_excerpt: You may choose to allow certain Google services, including services like Search or Gemini Apps, to access data from other Google services you use
changes.explanation: The policy now describes a mechanism allowing users to let services like Search or Gemini access data from other Google services such as Photos, Gmail, and Drive, in order to personalize content and ads. Previously the policy did not describe this cross-service data access feature.
changes.practical_effect: If enabled, a user's content in services like Gmail, Drive, or Photos can be used by other Google services such as Search or Gemini to personalize results and ads.

changes.title: Personalized ads can draw on content from Photos, Gmail, Drive if enabled
changes.new_excerpt: unless you choose to make data from these services available to other Google services that support personalized ads
changes.old_excerpt: We don\u2019t show you personalized ads based on your content from Drive, Gmail, or Photos.
changes.explanation: The prior blanket statement that Drive, Gmail, and Photos content is never used for personalized ads has been qualified with an exception for when a user opts to share this data with other Google services supporting personalized ads.
changes.practical_effect: Content from Gmail, Drive, or Photos could be used to personalize ads if a user enables data sharing between those services and ad-supporting services.

changes.title: Broader basis for personalized ads
changes.new_excerpt: we may also show you personalized ads based on your interests, activity, or personalized content from Google services
changes.old_excerpt: we may also show you personalized ads based on your interests and activity across Google services
changes.explanation: The description of what personalized ads can be based on was expanded from interests and activity to also include personalized content from Google services.
changes.practical_effect: Users may see ads influenced by a wider range of data, including personalized content generated by Google services, not just browsing interests and activity.

changes.title: New Personal Intelligence feature description
changes.new_excerpt: If you choose to allow certain services to process data from other services, including for features such as Personal Intelligence, the same data may be…
changes.explanation: A new feature called Personal Intelligence is introduced, which can use data from one Google service (such as an email) to personalize outputs in another (such as Search suggestions).
changes.practical_effect: Users who enable this feature may receive personalized suggestions in one Google service based on information drawn from another, such as emails informing search recommendations.

report.summary: Google's Privacy Policy was updated to describe new cross-service data sharing options, including a feature called Personal Intelligence, that let data from services like Gmail, Drive, and Photos be used by other services such as Search or Gemini to personalize content and, in some cases, ads. The previous blanket statement that Drive, Gmail, and Photos content is never used for ad personalization was qualified with an opt-in exception.</summary>

report.cosmetic_note: The only change replaces a spelled-out URL with a hyperlinked label text ("GitHub Subprocessors"), with no change in meaning or content.
report.summary: This update makes a purely cosmetic change, converting a plain-text URL into a hyperlinked label without altering any substantive terms.

changes.title: Cross-device activity used for non-account personalization
changes.new_excerpt: whether to show you more relevant search results or ads based on your activity across devices
changes.old_excerpt: whether to show you more relevant search results or ads based on your activity
changes.explanation: The policy now states that for users not signed in to a Google Account, data tied to a browser, application, or device identifier may be used to personalize search results or ads based on activity tracked across multiple devices, rather than just within a single browsing session or device as previously described.
changes.practical_effect: Even without signing in, a user's activity on one device may be linked and used to influence search results or ads shown on another device.

report.summary: Google updated its Privacy Policy to clarify that for signed-out users, activity-based personalization of search results and ads may occur across multiple devices, not just within a single session or device.

report.cosmetic_note: The only changes are removal of "Learn more" hyperlink text from two example paragraphs about Google Photos and Google Trends; the substantive descriptions of how data is used remain unchanged.
report.summary: The changes consist solely of removing "Learn more" link labels from two illustrative examples, with no alteration to the underlying policy content.

changes.title: New Korea-specific PIPA addendum added
changes.new_excerpt: This section applies to the extent that Anthropic is subject to the Personal Information Protection Act ("PIPA")
changes.explanation: A new addendum has been added specifically for users in the Republic of Korea, supplementing the main Privacy Policy under Korea's Personal Information Protection Act. It states this addendum controls over the main policy in case of inconsistency for Korean users.
changes.practical_effect: Users in South Korea now have an additional, more detailed set of disclosures governing how their personal data is collected, used, and transferred, which takes precedence over the general policy where the two conflict.

changes.title: New disclosure of identity verification data collection
changes.new_excerpt: Purpose: Identity verification, Fraud and abuse monitoring
changes.explanation: The addendum newly discloses that Anthropic collects name, birthdate, sex, a native-foreigner code, and duplication information (DI) for identity verification and fraud/abuse monitoring purposes, retained until account deletion.
changes.practical_effect: Korean users are now informed that additional identity-related data is being collected and retained specifically for verification and fraud prevention until they delete their account.

changes.title: New disclosure of delegated data processing to third parties
changes.new_excerpt: Anthropic delegates the processing of personal data as described here and below, and the delegatees may process personal data according to the purpose of the…
changes.explanation: The addendum discloses that Anthropic delegates certain personal data processing tasks to named third parties: Korea Credit Bureau for fraud/identity verification and Kim & Chang for domestic representative duties.
changes.practical_effect: Users' data may be processed by these named third-party organizations for the stated purposes, in addition to Anthropic itself.

changes.title: New disclosure of overseas transfer of identity data to Persona (US)
changes.new_excerpt: Anthropic delegates the processing of personal data to affiliates and third parties, all of whom are located overseas.
changes.explanation: The addendum discloses that identity-verification data (name, birthdate, sex, native-foreigner code, DI) is transferred to Persona, a company located in the United States, for fraud detection and identity verification, retained for 3 years under a specific PIPA legal basis.
changes.practical_effect: Korean users' identity data may be sent to and stored by a US-based company for up to three years as part of identity verification processing.

changes.title: New right to object to overseas data transfer
changes.new_excerpt: You may have the right to request that your personal data not be transferred overseas as described above.
changes.explanation: The addendum newly informs users they may request that their data not be transferred overseas by contacting Anthropic's privacy email or Data Protection Officer, but warns this may limit Anthropic's ability to provide services.
changes.practical_effect: Users can attempt to opt out of overseas data transfer, but doing so may result in reduced or unavailable service functionality.

changes.title: Change of Korea domestic representative and contact details
changes.new_excerpt: Email: anthropic_privacy@kimchang.com
changes.explanation: The domestic representative contact information for South Korea has changed from Bae, Kim & Lee LLC to Kim & Chang, including new phone number and email address.
changes.practical_effect: Users in South Korea seeking to contact the domestic representative about privacy matters must now use the new Kim & Chang contact details instead of the previous firm's contact information.

report.summary: Anthropic added a new Korea-specific PIPA addendum to its Privacy Policy detailing collection of identity-verification data, delegation of processing to third parties (Korea Credit Bureau, Kim & Chang), and overseas transfer of identity data to a US-based verification vendor (Persona), along with a user right to object to such transfers. The domestic representative in South Korea also changed from Bae, Kim & Lee LLC to Kim & Chang, with updated contact details."

report.cosmetic_note: All detected changes involve reordering of section labels/headings and navigation or page layout elements (e.g., menu labels, contact section headings, form-related text), with no changes to the substantive terms, rights, or obligations described in the policies.
report.summary: The changes consist solely of reformatting and relabeling of navigation/contact page elements; no substantive policy language was altered.

changes.title: Automatic sign-in via university single sign-on
changes.new_excerpt: the Platform may sign you in automatically. You can sign out at any time, and you will only be signed into an account
changes.explanation: The updated policy adds a new provision stating that if a user has an active single sign-on session with their university, the Platform may automatically log them in without a separate login step. It notes users can sign out and will only be signed into a pre-existing account.
changes.practical_effect: Users who are already logged into their university's single sign-on system may find themselves automatically signed into the Platform without taking any additional login action.

report.summary: The privacy policy adds a new section describing automatic sign-in through a user's university single sign-on session, noting users can sign out and will only access an existing account.
